events.summary: Resolve twelve queued CPU audit areas and review material disk-tool, arcade-port and engine updates
events.notes: Primary READMEs, build files, source/artifacts and current commits distinguish architecture-bearing native programs from HUNK containers, savestates, raw graphics, disk images and flux data. The C HUNK parser built and ran its usage path locally; the STTRANS.PRG primary artifact identifies as Atari ST M68K. Active-upstream review records UnifiedFloppyTool's ring/G71 evidence, Rolling Thunder's still-incomplete multi-CPU sync and Firestaff's bounded authentic door/inventory regressions without promoting any of them beyond their demonstrated scope.

events.summary: Promote five Atari VCS homebrew projects and a Watcom DOS disassembly tool
events.notes: Queue route: reviewed the complete canonical submodule list in milnak/atari-vcs-disassembly. Fresh-search routes and exact queries: GitHub repository search 'amstrad cpc disassembly', 'dos decompilation', and 'intellivision disassembly', followed by GitHub code search 'Intellivision CP1610 disassembly'. Reviewed candidate URLs: brpocock/Grizzards, DNSDEBRO/Climber5, DNSDEBRO/Pacman4K, chesterbr/2048-2600 and nanochess/Atomchess-6502 (promoted); nanochess/book-Atari, kreiach/8Blit and optixx/2600 (excluded only as aggregate project records; retained as discovery collections); fonic/wcdatool (promoted); SillyBudgieIndustries/vscode-dosbox-debug (deferred for capability verification). CPC results were already indexed; the Intellivision searches produced no new qualifying candidate.

events.summary: Resolve twelve queued CPU audit areas across six Amiga, Atari ST and DOS research projects
events.notes: Primary README, tree, source and Makefile review distinguishes data/media inputs from executable CPU provenance. It records CPU-not-applicable for data conversion/parsing, explicit 68000 guest emulation for lxa, an explicit m68k-atari-mint output for NiteCrawl, and no-evidence-found where DOS or Amiga platform labels would otherwise invite unsupported inference.

events.notes: Primary READMEs and source/build files established ARM firmware targets, analysed-binary CPUs, CPU-not-applicable data conversions, Z80 arcade listings and AmiXcom's 68020/AGA hardware floor. Active-upstream claims retain the projects' own validation limits.

events.summary: Resolve twelve queued CPU audit areas across arcade originals, VM-bytecode research and physical-media tooling

events.summary: Promote eight MSX, PC-98 and Atari reconstruction, restoration and archaeology-tooling projects
events.notes: Fresh-search route: GitHub repository/README search plus web GitHub-index search. Exact queries: 'Atari 8-bit disassembly source reconstruction', 'MSX disassembly reassembly reverse engineering', and 'PC-98 disassembly decompilation reverse engineering', including site:github.com variants. Reviewed candidate URLs: GuillianSeed/MetalGear (promoted), mcolom/arkanoid_msx_disasm (promoted), ValleyBell/PC98VNResearch (promoted), FuzionCD/lime-juice (promoted), tomyun/juice (duplicate predecessor lineage), nmlgc/ReC98 (promoted), nmlgc/np2debug (promoted), sidneycadot/Atari8bit_OSB-NTSC-ROM (promoted), fa8ntomas/blck-game-engine (promoted after source review), milnak/atari-vcs-disassembly (excluded as an aggregate discovery node pending component review), and Dalekamistoso/MSXDUMPTOOLS (excluded redistribution bundle). Existing ChoplifterReverse, planet and StarRaiders records were deduplicated before deep review.

events.summary: Resolve eleven queued source/target CPU audit areas across Mixup, ALIS and recovery/compression tooling
events.notes: Primary README/source review explicitly establishes m68k for DoDonPachi DaiOuJou through its documented 68000 bus-wrap handling. The other Mixup titles and the two decompiled compressors record no-evidence-found rather than platform inference; ALIS documents native platform-specific VM inputs and portable host builds without naming CPU targets; AmigaQB_extract is CPU-not-applicable because it parses backup data and restores files. The unresolved CPU-project queue falls from 164 to 157 while closing eleven distinct areas.

events.summary: Resolve ten queued CPU audit areas and review material NESRecomp, STDL and Firestaff advances
events.notes: Primary source/code and current MAME hardware drivers resolve six arcade-original CPUs plus BeerMon source/output architecture. The two cyxx cases record no-evidence-found or not-applicable instead of platform inference. Active review captures bounded cycle-accurate/rollback, STDL audio/timing and Firestaff runtime/save advances with their stated limitations.

The Windows build compiles embedded Musashi, custom OCS and game-address-specific host logic; this documents execution architecture, not a quality or AI assessment. Also reviewed Battle Squadron's separate playable Musashi host and incomplete no-Musashi native translation.

Routes: web queries site:github.com Amiga game disassembly reverse engineering reassemble 68000 source 2025 2026; site:github.com Amiga game reimplementation source reconstruction ASM 68k; site:github.com Atari ST game disassembly reassembly 68000 source; site:github.com Atari ST game reverse engineering port source reconstruction; GitHub repository queries amiga disassembly in:description, amiga reverse engineering in:description, atari st disassembly in:description, atari st reverse engineering in:description, amiga reassembled in:readme, atari ste disassembly in:readme. The obvious results were already tracked (including geogeo28's six ST titles, sarnau VT100, JOTD Xevious/Scramble, hitchhikr games, mnemo70 demos and the Uko-TAL scroller). Reviewed eight new primary READMEs and screened LibreROM's Mac-first roadmap; remaining search hits are unreviewed. No raw-result success rate is claimed.

events.notes: Compared the collection README with each of fourteen actual component directories and the first source-file sections. Three components were already catalogued. These eleven distinct source files identify the historical intro, trainer or tool and reconstruction attribution; build success, binary comparison, complete runtime behavior and minimum hardware remain unverified. The historical tool records represent reconstructed subjects rather than claiming modern utility or an original commercial binary match.
